Chapter 12 368
Summary
AWS offers a vast array of services that you can use to design and build decoupled and
distributed architectures for your applications. Depending on your business use case, moving
away from a monolithic architecture to a microservices-based, event-driven design provides
several benefits, including reduced single points of failure, independent component scalability,
and improved availability.
To design decoupled architectures, you need a way to separate your application components,
such as frontend and backend services. This is only possible if those components can
communicate in a manner that facilitates independent operation and scalability. The use of
message queuing systems like Amazon SQS plays a critical role in bringing this type of
architecture to life.
Furthermore, designing your application stack so that each component communicates
asynchronously and responds to events as they occur ensures that resources are only
consumed when required. Amazon EventBridge enables you to build such event-driven
applications, helping you avoid idle resources and unnecessary costs.
Finally, when designing complex, distributed, and decoupled architectures, the use of
orchestration services such as Amazon Step Functions gives you the ability to design
application workflows quickly and efficiently.
In the next chapter, you will learn how you can use AWS to analyze the vast array of data your
business collects and stores, both for auditing purposes as well as for specific application
requirements. AWS offers a number of different analytical tools enabling you to perform real-
time data ingestions, perform ad-hoc queries, and even Big Data analytics.

Analytics on AWS
Data is the ultimate currency of the 21st century. Businesses today can either gain a massive
competitive advantage through how they analyze and consume data—or, at worst, go
completely out of business due to data leaks and mismanagement. Companies use data to
understand their markets, identify trends, predict sales, and ultimately gain a competitive
edge.
Furthermore, in idx_83be6256 this era of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI),
understanding idx_31a72635 vast amounts of data has become easier. Organizations can now query their
data, identify complex patterns, and discover outliers much faster. Today's analytical tools,
powered by AI and ML, enable businesses to build solutions that deliver better customer
service, prevent fraud, identify and even predict technical issues or bugs in application code—
and much more.
AWS offers a vast array of analytical services, each designed for different use cases. Whether
you need to process streaming data in real time, run ad-hoc queries, or host an entire data
warehousing solution for your global enterprise, AWS has a service for it.
In this chapter, you will learn about these services, their use cases, and best practices for
configuring them for your specific needs—enabling you to ingest, store, and analyze your data
efficiently.
The following topics are discussed in this chapter:
Streaming data with Amazon Kinesis
Understanding your data structure with AWS Glue
Performing ad hoc analytics with Amazon Athena
•
•
•
Searching and processing large-scale data with Amazon OpenSearch Service and
Amazon EMR
Learning about business intelligence with Amazon Quick Suite
Streaming data with Amazon Kinesis
A wide range of applications today generate streaming data that must be captured, ingested,
processed, and idx_b1a874f2 analyzed in real time. Examples include logs generated idx_79d40099 by applications (used to
identify access patterns or errors), clickstream data from idx_a0026c0d websites (to uncover trends and
customer behaviors), and Internet of Things (IoT) data (used to monitor sensors, images,
videos, and other connected devices).
Organizations need a reliable mechanism to capture massive volumes of streaming data and
ingest it in real time. This data then needs to be processed and consumed by business
intelligence applications to provide reporting, analytics, and visualizations that support
critical decision-making.

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 12 370
chunks.content:
AWS offers Amazon Kinesis, a suite of fully managed, serverless services that lets you process
streaming data as it arrives. It enables real-time and near-real-time analytics in a cost-effective
manner—without idx_66a2897a the need to provision or manage any idx_e8625943 underlying infrastructure.
The Amazon Kinesis product suite comprises four key services:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon Kinesis Video Streams
Amazon Data Firehose
Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
In the coming sections, you will examine each of these services, starting with Amazon Kinesis
Data Streams and its core capabilities.
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
You can idx_0d36998d use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest and process continuous streams of data
in real time. Data is ingested into the stream from producers that capture information from a
wide range of sources, as shown in Figure 13.1:

chunks.heading: Chapter 13 374

Chapter 13 374
Figure 13.1: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
You can create idx_e2e187bb Kinesis data stream applications using the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) and
Amazon idx_c73dcf24 EC2 instances to read data idx_f35217c0 from the streams (known as consumers) and process it
according to your specific business use case. For example, you can use streaming data to build
real-time dashboards, perform anomaly detection to identify fraudulent activities, dynamically
adjust pricing, modify advertising strategies, and much more.
As illustrated in Figure 13.1, Kinesis Data Streams uses the concept of shards, which represent
units of capacity and contain data records within a stream. A stream can consist of multiple
shards, and the total capacity of the stream is the sum of all shard capacities. The overall cost is
determined by the number of shards provisioned, as you are charged per shard per hour.
An important feature of Amazon Kinesis is that data remains in the stream and is accessible for
up to 24 hours by default. This soft limit can be extended to 7 days using the extended data
retention feature. You can also enable long-term data retention, which allows data to be stored
for up to 365 days. This ensures that consuming applications have sufficient time to process all
incoming data streams.
While Amazon Kinesis Data Streams allows you to capture and process streaming data in real
time, it requires you to build and manage the consumer applications that process and store
that data. However, sometimes all you need is a reliable way to deliver large volumes of
streaming idx_2b523556 data directly into storage or analytics services without managing the underlying
infrastructure.
This is where Amazon Data Firehose becomes useful. Amazon Data Firehose automatically
delivers streaming data to a wide range of AWS services and external storage endpoints,
making it easier to load large amounts of data into storage services for later analysis.
375 Analytics on AWS
Amazon Data Firehose
Businesses need to ingest and load raw data into a wide range of technology services to
perform idx_1c8f9a36 analytics, store historical data for compliance and regulatory requirements, and feed
data into tools like Amazon OpenSearch Service for near real-time analytics using a variety of
business intelligence platforms.
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose can also deliver data to external third-party services such as
Datadog, New Relic, and Splunk, among others, enabling you to continue using the tools your
organization is already familiar with. The service can batch, process, compress, and transform
data before loading it into these third-party targets. You can also encrypt this data to
strengthen your overall security posture.
Kinesis Data Firehose buffers incoming data before delivering it to destinations such as

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 13 374
chunks.content:
Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, or Amazon OpenSearch Service. This buffering introduces a
small delay (typically around 30 to 60 seconds), depending on the buffer size and interval
settings. This is why Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is considered a near real-time data loading
service.
You can think of Amazon Kinesis Data Streams as a live news broadcast service. You process
data as soon as it's ingested. In contrast, Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is more like a news
highlights feed; you receive updates every minute, bundled and ready for easy consumption.
Amazon Kinesis idx_14a87337 Data Streams and Amazon Data Firehose are commonly used to process
streaming data such as application logs, clickstream data, and telemetry information.
However, these services are not designed for continuously streaming video feeds. For video
streaming workloads, AWS provides Amazon Kinesis Video Streams, which you will explore in
the next section.
Amazon Kinesis Video Streams
Businesses today stream a vast array of different content types, and this includes video footage
idx_537a7497 that needs to be analyzed, documented, processed, and used for live or on-demand viewing.
Amazon Kinesis Video Streams enables you to capture live video data from a wide range of
sources, including CCTV cameras, webcams, drones, and other sources.
Amazon Kinesis Video Streams can also be used to send non-video time-serialized data, such
as audio, radar, thermal imaging, and much more. Amazon Kinesis Video Streams will store
your raw footage in Amazon S3, ensuring high levels of durability for your data. You can then
search for and retrieve those footages based on devices and timestamps.
A key use case for Amazon Kinesis Video Streams is that you can use downstream services on
AWS to then analyze those footages and apply the data to real-world solutions. For example,
you can integrate your idx_c8a99295 application architecture to have Amazon Rekognition, a computer

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 13 376
chunks.content:
Chapter 13 376
vision machine learning service on AWS, identify objects, people, text, scenes, and activities in
the images and videos.
Figure 13.2 illustrates a use case for Amazon Kinesis Video Streams services:
Figure 13.2: Amazon Kinesis Video Streams
In this scenario, Amazon Rekognition is used to identify the license plate of any vehicle that
crosses the speed limit and interfaces with a backend database to send an email to the owner/
driver of a fine that needs to be paid for the violation.
Another idx_05f28325 example of using Amazon Kinesis Video Streams is for smart home devices such as
doorbells. Amazon Kinesis Video Streams can ingest, index, and live-play those streams to your
smartphone app, allowing you to monitor and communicate with the person knocking on the
door.
Some businesses may already use streaming frameworks in their on-premises environments
and want to migrate these workloads to AWS. To support open-source stream processing tools
such as Apache Flink, AWS provides Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink. This is a fully
managed service that allows you to run Flink applications without managing infrastructure
and is covered in the next section.
Amazon managed service for Apache Flink
Many businesses idx_cf388918 today use an open-source, real-time idx_ada0eaa7 stream processing engine called Apache
Flink to ingest and process large volumes of data, either in real time or in batches. The service
provides powerful capabilities for running complex computations on streaming data, such as
filtering, aggregating, and joining data streams with very low latency.
Rather than idx_2c41a01e designing, building, and managing your own expensive infrastructure to run this
streaming service, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink offers a pay-as-you-go model
where AWS handles all infrastructure management, scaling, and fault tolerance. You simply
write your Flink application code using SQL, Java, or Python to analyze data coming from
Kinesis Data Streams or Kinesis Data Firehose, without the need to manage servers or clusters.
377 Analytics on AWS
Businesses store vast amounts of data in a variety of formats and locations, including
databases and spreadsheets. Often, this data needs to be extracted, transformed into a format
suitable for analysis, and then loaded into services that can perform analytics and support the
creation of business intelligence solutions. The next section introduces you to AWS Glue, a
service idx_fa784ad4 designed specifically for this purpose.
Understanding your data structure with AWS Glue
AWS Glue is a idx_fa819110 serverless Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) service. Businesses idx_22cad2fa can use
AWS Glue to discover, prepare, enrich, clean, and idx_aec7755a transform data so that downstream services
can easily consume it.

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 13 376
chunks.content:
The service offers the ability to crawl your raw datasets and discover their structure, also
known idx_15812598 as a schema. For example, AWS Glue can analyze CSV files to identify column names
and their data types (such as string, number, or Boolean). This makes it easier to ingest the
idx_1726d081 data into analytics and business intelligence (BI) tools for further analysis and visualization.
You can use the crawler to scan various data repositories, classify datasets, and infer their
schemas. The resulting metadata is then stored in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, which can be
used to automatically generate ETL scripts that transform, flatten, or enrich your datasets. You
can also define events or schedules to run crawlers regularly against your ingested datasets as
batch jobs, ensuring your data remains continuously prepared for analysis by downstream
services such as Amazon QuickSight and Amazon Athena.
While idx_6617261b some customers continuously stream, process, and analyze idx_3d44fd22 data in real time, others may
only need a cost-effective approach to run ad-hoc queries against data that has been captured
over time. In such cases, hosting a fully-fledged database or data warehouse solution like
Amazon Redshift can be excessive. The next section introduces you to Amazon Athena, a
service designed to run ad-hoc queries directly against data stored in Amazon S3, without the
need to provision or manage traditional database infrastructure.
Performing ad hoc analytics with Amazon Athena
Many companies store data as files in object storage services such as Amazon S3. Much of this
data idx_d2effedb is only occasionally accessed idx_68c297a0 for point-in-time analysis and then stored for historical
reference. In other words, these datasets do not need to be stored in active idx_bb3d3bbd databases such idx_2617ec9a as
Amazon RDS or NoSQL databases like Amazon DynamoDB, since the data is not regularly
queried.
Nevertheless, ad-hoc analysis of such data, for example, running daily batch jobs or
performing historical analysis, may still be required. In such cases, provisioning entire

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 13 378
chunks.content:
Chapter 13 378
databases and ingesting large datasets for a one-time or infrequent analysis can be
unnecessary and costly.
AWS offers Amazon Athena, a fully idx_0cc5e87e managed, serverless query service that allows you to
interactively analyze raw data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL (Structured Query
Language). You idx_a63835bd don't need to provision or manage any infrastructure, nor do you need to spin
up expensive database instances to perform ad-hoc queries.
Amazon idx_3b1f889f Athena uses Presto, an open-source SQL query engine designed for running fast,
interactive queries. It supports ANSI SQL, enabling you to work with features like large joins,
window functions, and arrays.
With idx_3b471113 Amazon Athena, you can run queries idx_4c0c2aa8 against structured and semi-structured datasets. To
perform your queries, you must create a database table within Athena that defines the schema
of your raw data stored in Amazon S3. This means Athena only needs to understand the data
structure; the data itself remains in S3. Athena simply uses the table definition to query the
underlying raw data, without needing to move or ingest it.
You can also use AWS Glue, which you learned about in the previous section, to crawl your raw
data in Amazon S3 and automatically generate the required schema for your Athena tables.
Once your tables are registered, you can run SQL SELECT statements to query them, and you
can even store query results in Amazon S3 in a location of your choice. A typical use case where
Belly Brew Co. Limited might use Amazon Athena is if it needs to run a query like "What were
our top 10 Kombucha flavors last month?"
In the next idx_d27c15f7 section, you will learn about Amazon OpenSearch Service and Amazon EMR,
which idx_339c0971 offer additional capabilities for large-scale search and big data analytics.
Searching and processing large-scale data with
Amazon OpenSearch Service and Amazon EMR
While idx_c501095c Amazon Athena is designed to analyze idx_9656e2ef static and historical idx_4be7d515 data directly from idx_415b6cec Amazon
S3, there are times when you idx_af3b75c2 need a robust, ultra-fast search solution capable idx_589d2b69 of delivering
results within milliseconds. That's where Amazon OpenSearch Service comes in.
For example, you might use Athena to run a query like, "What were our top 10 Kombucha
flavors last month?" Whereas with OpenSearch, you could perform a search like "Show me all
error logs idx_2959efea containing the word 'timeout' from the last hour."
Amazon OpenSearch Service is designed for searching, filtering, and visualizing log or text
data in real time. It scales seamlessly, supporting up to 25 petabytes of attached storage and up
to 1002 data nodes running on Amazon EC2 instances.
379 Analytics on AWS
OpenSearch enables you to perform full-text search, log analytics, and clickstream analytics.

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 13 378
chunks.content:
The traditional deployment model requires provisioning the necessary EC2 instances within
an OpenSearch cluster. However, AWS also offers a serverless edition, allowing you to run
petabyte-scale workloads without configuring, managing, or scaling any infrastructure.
Additionally, Amazon OpenSearch Service includes a vector engine that provides vector
storage and search capabilities for ML-augmented applications and generative AI solutions—
without the need to host and manage your own vector database.
Another service idx_5cf62505 offered by AWS is Amazon EMR (Elastic MapReduce). This service enables
you to process big data analytics using industry-recognized open-source frameworks, such as
Apache Spark, Apache Hive, Apache HBase, and Presto.
Amazon idx_b8f2df87 EMR automatically provisions and idx_eb22bdb1 scales the required infrastructure idx_4a9e223d to run petabyte-
scale idx_c77dfaa6 analytics workloads efficiently. The idx_2f2f636a service supports running workloads idx_3042cd52 on Amazon EC2
instances, Amazon EKS clusters, and even on on-premises environments through Amazon
EMR on AWS Outposts.
While streaming, loading, analyzing, and searching data form a substantial part of a business's
data analytics functions, the ability to visualize that data, enabling decision-makers to take
real action, is equally critical. The next section introduces you to Amazon QuickSight, AWS's BI
solution.
Learning about business intelligence with Amazon
Quick
Amazon Quick is a idx_2deff0ed collection of tools and capabilities that provides traditional idx_92202534 business
intelligence services enhanced idx_a63cd056 with modern AI assistance. It enables you to connect to a wide
range of data sources, whether on-premises data stores, AWS databases, cloud storage services
such as Amazon RDS and Amazon S3, or external SaaS and B2B applications.
You can use Amazon Quick to process and transform raw data, create rich visualization
dashboards, and generate insightful reports. These insights help you better understand your
organization's operations, sales performance, profitability, customer acquisition trends, and
much more.
Amazon idx_f4b678ad Quick includes five core services that work seamlessly together:
Amazon QuickSight – for data visualization and interactive dashboards
Amazon QuickFlows – for workflow automation
Amazon QuickAutomate – for process optimization
•
•
•

chunks.content:
Chapter 13 380
Amazon Quick Index – for data discovery
Amazon QuickResearch – for comprehensive analysis
In addition idx_14892306 to its AI integration, you can deploy idx_0adc9901 extensions for familiar tools such as web
browsers, Slack, and Microsoft Office applications.
Now that you know about the core analytical services offered by AWS, it's time to put your
learning into practice. In the next section, you will complete a series of exercises to gain hands-
on experience with some of AWS's analytical tools.
Project task 13 – Analyzing Belly Brew Co. Limited's
kombucha casks for pH balance
In Chapter 1, you idx_19f23f00 were introduced idx_ac7dab73 to a fictitious company called Belly Brew Co. Limited, which
is a manufacturer and supplier of gut-friendly beverages across the UK. The company supplies
a large range of these beverages to supermarkets, grocery stores, restaurants, cafes, and hotels.
One business requirement mentioned was the issue of assuring the health and safety of the
kombucha casks that are fermenting for several days before being bottled and shipped.
Specifically, the pH level of the beverage must adhere to a specific range of 2.5 to 3.5.
Currently, the manufacturing plants use outdated pH analyzer equipment that records the pH
level of each cask at regular intervals and produces a report in CSV format. This report must be
printed out and manually reviewed to identify any casks that need to be removed from
distribution whose PH levels are outside of the acceptable range. The reports must be reviewed
daily, and the results of the analysis must be completed by 5 PM daily.
You have been tasked with designing a solution that will automatically analyze the data and
produce a report of all casks that must be removed from the batch each day.
This idx_6591cef7 project task will introduce idx_1a5bd00f you to the architectural concepts and then provide step-by-
step instructions to build a solution in your AWS account that the company can use. This will
only be a partial solution, as the supplier of the pH meters will need to update their software to
deliver the CSV reports directly to your application stack. As such, you will also appreciate that
solutioning may involve working with third parties too.
The proposed architecture
The project briefing provided earlier and in Chapter 1 explained that the PH analyzer tool can
produce idx_5615a284 CSV files with reports of the PH levels of all casks being monitored.
Given that the CSV files can be hosted on a file share, you can redirect the repository to an
Amazon S3 bucket, which could be used to host the files for analysis. You have also been
•
•
381 Analytics on AWS
informed that the analysis needs to be carried out every day and the results available at 5 PM
daily.
In previous idx_0b4d1696 chapters, you have learned about various AWS services that can be used to help you

chunks.content:
automate this requirement and perform the analysis. For example:
Amazon S3 to host idx_39a1fce3 the CSV files. You can also use the same bucket to host the results in
a separate folder.
Amazon Athena can be idx_a245d196 used to run queries against the raw data and identify the casks
that need to be removed. Given that the analysis task needs to be performed only once
a day, there is no requirement to store the data in a database like Amazon RDS.
Database solutions like Amazon RDS would add complexity and incur unnecessary
costs because you pay for every second that the database instance is in a running state.
This is unlike Amazon Athena, where you only pay for the cost of performing the
queries.
AWS Lambda to perform idx_c802f08a the actual analysis by identifying the raw data and invoking
the query in Amazon Athena. You are using Lambda because it can be used to run the
query in Amazon Athena automatically if triggered by another service, such as Amazon
EventBridge. The Lambda service is also designed to ensure that the analysis is stored
in date order to ensure that future audits would be easy to perform if required, thereby
maintaining a date-ordered trail.
Amazon EventBridge configured idx_55454c2d with a scheduled rule to trigger the Lambda function
at 5 PM

The idx_07dcbad8 following outlines the key architectural design pattern for this solution, as shown by the
numbering in the diagram:
The CSV data is uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket that you will create for this project
The CSV file will be stored in a folder called rawdata. In a real-world scenario, you
would work with the vendor of the pH analysis tool to ensure that the CSV files are
delivered directly to the S3 bucket you have created. Additional folders would also be
required. These include the athena folder, which allows Amazon Athena to store query
results and temporary files, and the processed folder, which will store the results of the
query analysis.
You will configure Amazon Athena to point to the S3 bucket that contains this raw data.
As part of the configuration, you will specify the athena folder you created in Step 2 as
the location for query results. In addition, you will create a database. This database is
used to store the table definition so that Amazon Athena understands the structure of
the raw data stored in the CSV file. Remember that you do not import the data into
Amazon Athena. Instead, Athena uses the schema definition and queries the raw data
directly from Amazon S3.
You will configure an IAM role to ensure that the Lambda function has the required
permissions to access both the Amazon S3 bucket and Amazon Athena
When triggered, the Lambda function will capture the current date and determine the
path of the raw data. This ensures that the analysis is performed on the current day's
CSV file. The Lambda function will then invoke a query in Amazon Athena to analyze
this raw data. Query results are stored in the athena folder in the Amazon S3 bucket.
Once the analysis is complete, the resulting dataset highlighting all casks that fall
outside the pH range is written to the processed folder in the same S3 bucket.
To trigger the Lambda function at 5 PM each day, you will configure Amazon
EventBridge with a scheduled event rule. At 5 PM, this rule will automatically invoke
the Lambda function.
Now that idx_fb4f7057 you have reviewed the core architectural design pattern, it's time to build out the
solution. The next section provides details on where you can access the Python code for this
task.

Summary
Data is the new currency for businesses, and the ability to analyze large volumes of data in the
shortest possible time is critical for any company. AWS offers a wide range of analytical tools
designed to help you stream, ingest, process, transform, and analyze your datasets. You have a
wide range of tools available at your disposal, many of which are fully managed, requiring no
infrastructure services to be managed by the customer.
You can use streaming tools like Amazon Kinesis that allow you to process and analyze data in
real-time. Services like Amazon Data Firehose can be used to load data onto a wide range of
AWS and third-party services, including Amazon S3, Redshift, Splunk, and much more.
If you need to perform ad-hoc queries against your data in Amazon S3, you have access to
Amazon Athena – a service you can use to perform ad-hoc analysis of your data. You can use
Amazon Glue to perform ETL jobs and discover the structure of the schema of your data.
d.

403 Analytics on AWS
Finally, you can use Amazon Quick to perform business intelligence analysis and build a
visualization dashboard and reporting for your organization.
The ability to understand data is critical for any business. However, in addition to that, the
ability to query data in a manner that is more human and easily digestible is just as important.
In addition, using past historical data to predict trends and make recommendations is a
powerful tool for any organization competing in today's global marketplace. AWS offers a wide
range of machine learning and artificial intelligence services that can help you perform trend
analysis, predict consumer behavior, and access information hidden in big data sets in a matter
of minutes. These topics are discussed in the next chapter.
In this chapter, we explored how AWS analytics services help businesses stream, prepare,
query, search, process, and visualize data using services such as Amazon Kinesis, AWS Glue,
Amazon Athena, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon EMR, and Amazon QuickSight. In the
next chapter, you will build on that data foundation by looking at AWS machine learning and
artificial intelligence services that can recognize images, convert text to speech, transcribe
audio, translate text, extract information from documents, analyze sentiment, and support
custom model development.

Machine Learning and Artificial
Intelligence
Machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) have taken the world by storm. Now
considered cutting-edge and among the most impactful technologies of our time, it has
become almost imperative for anyone pursuing a career in cloud computing to be familiar with
the wide range of AI and ML services available on modern cloud platforms—and to understand
how to use and support many of their managed AI/ML offerings.
Furthermore, with Generative AI rapidly transforming businesses and driving major gains in
efficiency and productivity, now is the ideal time to learn how these tools work and how to
build solutions around them. Companies are actively seeking expertise in GenAI services:
understanding customer interactions and sentiment, building chatbots that deliver human-
like conversations, and performing ultra-fast translations, transcriptions, and summarizations.
In this chapter, you will be introduced to a wide range of AI/ML services. For the AWS Certified
Cloud Practitioner exam, it is imperative that you understand these technologies at a high level
and are familiar with their primary use cases.
The topics covered in this chapter include:
Recognizing images, videos, and text with Amazon Rekognition
Converting text to speech with Amazon Polly
Using AWS services for transcription, translation, and text extraction
Understanding sentiment with Amazon Comprehend
Building your own models with Amazon SageMaker
•
•
•
•
•
Recognizing images, videos, and text with Amazon
Rekognition
Amazon Rekognition is idx_eb42485a a fully managed service that enables you to add computer vision
capabilities to your applications. You can use Amazon Rekognition to analyze images and video
files stored in Amazon S3 buckets.
Amazon Rekognition can detect objects and text in images and video, as well as compare faces,
perform facial analysis, and identify attributes, such as age, gender, and emotions.
Several idx_1fc29897 use cases include:
Searchable and labeled media libraries
Face-based identity verification systems
Detection idx_4a4e0d56 of personal protective equipment (PPE)
Celebrity recognition
Identification of unsafe content
Text idx_c3487c36 detection, and much more
Another capability of Amazon Rekognition idx_8b1514bf is Face Liveness. Many applications require live
verification using your mobile phone. For example, applying for a new passport or idx_b03798d5 completing
KYC (Know Your Customer) verification. In addition to uploading identity documents, you
are often required to log in to a web app using your mobile device and camera, where the app
scans your face as part of the live verification process.
Amazon Rekognition can detect whether the verification is being performed by a live person or
if a bad actor is attempting to spoof the system using digital photos, digital videos, or 3D

recognition and analysis.
While Amazon idx_fbe13b1f Rekognition can detect text embedded in images, it is not designed to offer a
complete text extraction and analysis service. AWS offers a wide range of other services such as
being able to extract text from pages of handwritten notes. Also, you may have text-based
documents that need to be converted to speech for audio books or for converting voice
narrations to text using a transcription service. In the next section, you will learn about

Chapter 14 408
Converting text to speech with Amazon Polly
Amazon Polly is an idx_f37b0a7c artificial intelligence service that uses deep learning to synthesize speech
into a human-like voice with just text inputs. You can select from a wide range of voices across
different accents and languages for both genders.
You can send your text data to Amazon Polly via API calls and have it immediately converted to
an audio stream, which you can play back as part of your application. Amazon Polly supports
standard audio formats like MP3.
Amazon Polly also idx_1c9a9725 offers Neural Text-to-Speech (NTTS) voices that support features like
Newscaster idx_18422dc8 speaking styles, enabling the delivery of flash news updates by TV and radio
newscaster organizations.
With Amazon Polly, you can also use custom lexicons to modify pronunciation for particular
words, use acronyms, and neologisms. To customize pronunciations, you can upload an XML
file with lexical entries. For example, some TTS systems pronounce the common English word
"often" incorrectly as "off-ten." Any time Polly encounters that word in your speech output, it
will use your custom pronunciation.
An example lexicon XML file is provided as follows:
<lexicon version="1.0"
xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/01/pronunciation-lexicon"
alphabet="ipa"
xml:lang="en-US">
<lexeme>
<grapheme>often</grapheme>
<!-- Correct pronunciation: "aw-fn" -->
<phoneme>ˈɔːfən</phoneme>
</lexeme>
</lexicon>
Notice how you can use the <phoneme> element to explicitly define the correct pronunciation.
This allows Amazon Polly to speak words exactly the way you intend, ensuring natural-
sounding and accurate text-to-speech output—even for words that are commonly
mispronounced.
You can use Amazon Polly idx_0caa704f for a wide range of voice applications, such as interactive voice
response (IVR) systems, educational idx_49a8a007 content narration, accessibility tools, real-time

announcements, audiobook generation, and creating natural-sounding voices for websites and
mobile apps.
After looking at how Amazon Polly turns text into speech, it is useful to look at services that
work in the other direction or with related language-processing tasks, such as converting
speech to text, translating content, and extracting text from documents.
Using AWS services for transcription, translation,
and text extraction
AWS provides several AI services that help you process spoken, written, and document-based
content. Amazon Transcribe converts speech into text, Amazon Translate converts text
between languages, and Amazon Textract extracts text and structured data from documents
and images.
Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Transcribe is a idx_cf42a789 fully managed automatic speech-to-text transcription service. You

can use Amazon Transcribe either as a standalone service—by pointing it to your audio files
stored in Amazon S3—or integrate it directly into your own transcription applications. This is
particularly useful when you need on-demand transcription of streaming audio, such as for
closed captioning, thanks to its deep learning technology.
Amazon Transcribe can help you extract business insights from meetings, customer calls, and
video files. You can also use it to automatically transcribe clinical conversations, and the
service is fully HIPAA compliant. For added privacy, you can have sensitive and personally
identifiable information (PII) automatically idx_f61d9311 redacted from your transcripts, ensuring
compliance with regulatory requirements.
There are no upfront idx_5695e5c6 costs or infrastructure charges. You can access the service on demand, and
you only pay for the seconds of audio transcribed, billed monthly.
Next, you will learn about Amazon Translate.
Amazon Translate
Amazon Translate is a idx_18cb2f11 text translation service that enables you to perform high-quality
translations. The service uses advanced machine learning technologies to enable you to
translate unstructured text and documents across multiple languages. You can build
applications and solutions that leverage Amazon Translate to automatically translate web
pages, meeting minutes, technical reports, knowledge bases, posts, and more.

Amazon Translate supports multiple languages and can auto-detect the source language.

You can use Amazon idx_695bd486 Translate to perform real-time translations or perform batch translation
jobs for a large collection of documents up to 5 GB in size. Batch processing is ideal for short
documents, social media postings, user reviews, and any other tasks not requiring real-time
translations.
Next, you will learn about another service that allows you to capture text data from a wide
range of document formats, including printed text, handwriting, and layout elements.
Amazon Textract
Many companies manually idx_1ff5da9d extract data from scanned documents, images, PDFs, tables, and idx_058de185
forms using a wide range of tools and optical character recognition (OCR) software.
However, often these software solutions are not adequate for every use case and require
manual configurations whenever the source is changed, such as changes in the form layout of a
PDF document.
Amazon Textract uses machine learning to read and process any type of document or image
and can extract text data accurately from a wide range of sources, including tables and
handwritten documents.

The extracted data can then be used to update backend databases. For example, the extracted
payslip data in Figure 14.2 can be ingested into an accounting application to complete the
annual tax return calculations.
Amazon idx_48b9cc61 Textract can also preserve the data structure stored in tabular formats during
extraction, ensuring that context remains intact and making it ideal for extracting information
from financial records, medical records, and any data in a column-row format.
Amazon Textract idx_ea95d77b can also detect text in handwritten documents and notes. It can detect
signatures on any document or image, enabling you to leverage the service for processing loan
application forms, claim forms, and much more.
In the next section, you will learn about an Amazon AI service that enables you to understand
the context and meaning of your textual data. This is particularly useful when you need to
perform sentiment analysis, for example, how customers feel about the customer service they
receive from your helpdesk team.
